fact: The infoDev/World Bank report states that the Sudanese national ICT strategy was formulated in June 1999, focused on technology infrastructure, human resources, software industry, Arabic content and geo-information.
The report states that a high-level ministerial committee was formed in June 1999 to oversee implementation of the national ICT strategy.
The ITU Academy repository, which lists strategies countries have adopted, records Sudan's National ICT Strategy 2021-2025 with no date of adoption; the document's published date (2025) is used.
The repository gives the National ICT Strategy's time frame as 2021-2025; the document's published date (2025) is used as the date of the statement.

The repository names the National Information Center (NIC) as lead and owner of the strategy, with the Ministry of Communications and Digital Transformation among other stakeholders; the document's published date (2025) is used.
The repository states no budget line for the strategy and lists the African Development Bank only as a stakeholder; the document's published date (2025) is used.
The repository gives evidence of implementation and the monitoring and evaluation framework for Sudan's strategy as N/A; the document's published date (2025) is used.

The ESCWA profile reports that an ICT strategy exists in Sudan, adopted in 2007 as the information society strategy within the 2007-2031 quarter-century plan, after the 2001-2006 national strategy for the information industry.
The profile says five-year information society strategy plans for 2007-2011 and then 2012-2016 were adopted; the current one runs to 2016 (document dated 2013-01-01).
The profile names the National Council for Strategic Planning as the government agency in charge of the ICT strategy (document dated 2013-01-01).
The profile rates the pace of implementation of the ICT strategy as 'Good', citing no targets or published report (document dated 2013-01-01).
